samples.summary: New login-error UI (LOGIN_ERRORS map + generic fallback + page wiring of ?error=) has no test at all
samples.evidence: login-form.tsx adds an `error` prop, a `LOGIN_ERRORS` code→message map, a `GENERIC_LOGIN_ERROR` fallback for unknown codes, and a `role="alert"` element; login/page.tsx wires `useSearchParams().get("error")` into it. This is the entire user-visible half of the new OAuth-state refusal path (backend redirects to `/login?error=oauth_state`). Grep for `login-form`/`LoginForm` in packages/frontend returns only login-form.tsx, app/login/page.tsx and README.md — no test file. The frontend has a running vitest lane with many component tests (e.g. packages/frontend/tests/components/theme-provider.test.tsx), so this is not an untestable area. Nothing would fail if the alert were never rendered, if the `oauth_state` key were misspelled (silently degrading every user to the generic message), or if page.tsx stopped passing the param.

samples.summary: No test pins that CliLoginConfirmMiddleware is actually registered for GET /auth/github
samples.evidence: AuthModule.configure() is new and is the only thing that makes the confirmation gate run. cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts instantiates the middleware directly (`new CliLoginConfirmMiddleware()`) and never goes through the Nest module, and github-auth.guard.spec.ts fabricates `__cliConfirmed` on a plain object. So if the `forRoutes({ path: 'auth/github', ... })` wiring were dropped or pointed at the wrong path, every backend spec stays green while CLI login silently degrades to a browser login (the guard's else branch). The guard spec's own comment claims to be pinning wiring, but it only pins the guard's half.
searchedFor: Glob packages/backend/src/**/*.spec.ts for a module-level/e2e auth spec

samples.summary: Confirm-cookie mismatch test uses different-length strings, so it cannot distinguish a real comparison from a length-only check
samples.evidence: `run({ ... confirm: 'attacker-minted' }, { [CLI_CONFIRM_COOKIE]: 'victims-cookie' })` compares a 15-char value against a 14-char value. `timingSafeEqualStr` short-circuits on `bufA.length !== bufB.length`, so this test passes even if the byte comparison were removed entirely. No test supplies an equal-length, different-valued confirm/cookie pair — the case an attacker would actually produce.

samples.summary: The non-web, unknown/expired state-token branch (BadRequestException) lost its only coverage in this diff
samples.evidence: The previous spec's `falls back to web flow when state token is not CLI` test was deleted and replaced by the web-flow describe block. The new else branch (`isWebOAuthState` false → consumeState → throw BadRequestException 'CLI login state expired or invalid') is now untested: grepping auth.controller.spec.ts for `BadRequestException` / 'CLI login state expired' returns no matches. Likewise the `port < 1024 || port > 65535` throw inside that branch has no test.

samples.summary: New oauth-state module has no dedicated spec; cookie options (path '/auth', secure-in-production) and timingSafeEqualStr are untested
samples.evidence: No packages/backend/src/auth/oauth-state.spec.ts exists (Glob of packages/backend/src/auth/*.ts and grep for 'oauth-state' shows importers only: auth.controller.ts, github-auth.guard.ts, cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts, auth.controller.spec.ts). github-auth.guard.spec.ts asserts only `{ httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'lax' }` via objectContaining — `path: '/auth'`, `maxAge`, and the NODE_ENV-dependent `secure` flag are asserted nowhere, and `timingSafeEqualStr` (also used by the CLI-confirm middleware) has no direct test for equal-length-different-value.

samples.summary: loginErrorUrl's trailing-slash normalization and missing-FRONTEND_URL fallback are never exercised
samples.evidence: The spec's ConfigService mock always returns 'http://localhost:5173' (no trailing slash), so `.replace(/\/+$/, '')` and the `?? ''` fallback in loginErrorUrl are dead under test — the redirect assertions would be identical if both were deleted.

samples.summary: formatCsv's neutralizeFormulas:false path is only covered end-to-end, never as a unit
samples.evidence: Grep for `formatCsv(` shows every call in packages/cli/test/output.test.ts passes `{ neutralizeFormulas: true }`; the false path is only reached via packages/cli/test/sheets-export.test.ts's `--raw` case. Also no test asserts that `format(data, 'csv')` (the render dispatcher, which hardcodes neutralizeFormulas: true) neutralizes — output.test.ts's dispatcher case uses `[{a: 1}]`.

samples.summary: The stated motivation for InvalidFormatError (a structured INVALID_FORMAT code) is unasserted at the content-format call sites
samples.evidence: parseNotesContentFormat / parseSlidesContentFormat / parseContentFormat now throw InvalidFormatError specifically so callers see `code: 'INVALID_FORMAT'`, but notes-content.test.ts:43, slides-content.test.ts:144 and docs-content.test.ts:75 only assert `/Invalid --format/` on the message — identical to the plain `new Error` they replaced. Swapping back to a bare Error would not fail any test.

samples.summary: State cookie clearing on the refusal paths is not asserted
samples.evidence: auth.controller.spec.ts asserts `res.clearCookie('wafflebase_oauth_state', ...)` only in the success test ('signs in when the state matches the cookie'). The mismatch / no-cookie / repeated-state tests assert only the redirect and `res.cookie` not being called, so a regression that left the stale state cookie set on refusal would go unnoticed.

finding.summary: New login-error UI (LOGIN_ERRORS map + generic fallback + page wiring of ?error=) has no test at all
finding.evidence: login-form.tsx adds an `error` prop, a `LOGIN_ERRORS` code→message map, a `GENERIC_LOGIN_ERROR` fallback for unknown codes, and a `role="alert"` element; login/page.tsx wires `useSearchParams().get("error")` into it. This is the entire user-visible half of the new OAuth-state refusal path (backend redirects to `/login?error=oauth_state`). Grep for `login-form`/`LoginForm` in packages/frontend returns only login-form.tsx, app/login/page.tsx and README.md — no test file. The frontend has a running vitest lane with many component tests (e.g. packages/frontend/tests/components/theme-provider.test.tsx), so this is not an untestable area. verdict.reason: Verified in-tree: login-form.tsx:15-33,48-55 defines LOGIN_ERRORS (key `oauth_state`), GENERIC_LOGIN_ERROR fallback, and a conditional role="alert" message; app/login/page.tsx:15,49 feeds useSearchParams().get("error") into it. No test anywhere exercises this. Repo-wide greps for LoginForm/login-form, for the literal message strings, and for `oauth_state` return only the component, the page, README/docs, and BACKEND specs (auth.controller.spec.ts, github-auth.guard.spec.ts) which cover the redirect emission, not the frontend rendering. No frontend test mounts the /login route (grep for `/login`/initialEntries in packages/frontend shows only App.tsx route registration and Navigate redirects), no *.spec.tsx exists in the frontend, and packages/frontend/tests has no `alert`/`error=` matches. CLI login tests cover an unrelated device-code flow. The frontend has a working vitest component lane with MemoryRouter-based tests (workspace-settings.test.tsx:83, document-analytics.test.tsx:20), so the area is testable. Nothing would fail if the alert never rendered, the `oauth_state` key were misspelled (silently degrading all users to the generic message), or the page stopped passing the param — a clear user-visible behavior change with zero coverage.

finding.summary: The renamed `__oauthState` → `opts.state` forwarding in GitHubStrategy.authenticate has no test at all
finding.evidence: The diff renames the request-attached state key from `__cliStateToken` to `__oauthState` in `github.strategy.ts:61-67`, and this is now the single hinge of the whole CSRF design (both CLI and browser states reach GitHub only through it). `github.strategy.spec.ts` (read in full, 119 lines) tests only endpoint resolution — it never constructs a request or asserts `super.authenticate` received `state`. Grep for `__oauthState` across packages/backend/src returns only the guard, the guard spec (which asserts the guard *sets* it) and the strategy itself; no test asserts the strategy *reads* that key. If the two sides ever spelled the key differently, every login would reach GitHub stateless and the new callback guard would reject every callback, with a fully green backend suite.

verdict.reason: The claim that the `__oauthState` → `opts.state` forwarding has no test is false. `packages/backend/src/auth/github.strategy.spec.ts` is 180 lines (not 119 as claimed) and contains a `describe('GitHubStrategy state forwarding')` block dedicated to exactly this behavior. It spies on the prototype-chain owner of `authenticate` (spec:137-154) so that `super.authenticate` at github.strategy.ts:67 is intercepted, builds a real request object, invokes the real `GitHubStrategy.authenticate`, and captures the options passed to super (spec:158-164). Test 1 (spec:166-172) sets `{ __oauthState: 'web.deadbeef' }` and asserts `opts?.state === 'web.deadbeef'` and that the caller's `scope` survives; test 2 (spec:174-178) asserts no `state` property is set when no guard ran, covering the `if (state)` branch at github.strategy.ts:64. The test is not over-mocked — the strategy under test is a real instance and only passport's base `authenticate` is stubbed to prevent the redirect. The precise failure mode the finding describes (the two sides spelling the key differently) would fail spec:169, and the guard side is pinned by github-auth.guard.spec.ts:72,100,111 asserting the guard writes `req.__oauthState`.

finding.summary: The confirmation page's preservation of `nonce` and `port` into the Continue href is untested
finding.evidence: `renderConfirmPage` re-encodes `mode`, `port`, `nonce` and `confirm` into the Continue link (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:100-103); that link is the only way the CLI's per-attempt nonce survives the new confirmation hop to the guard. In `cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts` the page-rendering test (line 43-56) passes NO nonce and asserts only `Continue` and `confirm=<secret>`; the test that does supply a nonce (line 58) takes the already-confirmed branch and never inspects any HTML. So `if (nonce) params.set('nonce', nonce)` and the port round-trip are unasserted: drop the nonce from the href and the CLI login silently breaks (loopback refuses with 'no `state`') while every test stays green.

verdict.reason: A test asserting exactly the claimed-missing behavior exists: cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts:67-84 ('carries the CLI port and nonce into the Continue link') drives the middleware down the unconfirmed branch with mode=cli, port=49152 and a 64-char nonce, extracts the href from the rendered HTML, un-escapes &, parses it with URLSearchParams and asserts mode==='cli', port==='49152' and nonce===the supplied nonce. Dropping `if (nonce) params.set('nonce', nonce)` (middleware.ts:101) or the port entry (line 100) makes those assertions fail, so the described mutation would not stay green. The finding's cited line numbers are stale: line 58 is a doc comment, the already-confirmed-branch test is at 86-100, and the reviewer evidently missed the intervening href test.
